reply.summary: Researched ADR-008 (Rust for the product, TypeScript confined to the pipeline) and wrote docs/designs/008-rust-for-the-product/01-research.md. Verified all fixed framework choices against primary sources as of Nov 2026: cargo workspaces (cargo check --workspace, flat-members glob, workspace inheritance), clap 4.6.7, axum 0.8.9/0.9-in-dev, sqlx 0.9 (now under transact-rs), Tauri v2 (2.12 current, stable since the tauri-2.0 release), TOML v1.1.0, and toml_edit for format-preserving codecs. Applied three lenses: prior art (kanata, xremap, Modrinth App, Goverlay, Heroic, JSON Schema Test Suite), platform notes (Proton compatdata prefixes, WebView2 distribution, WebKitGTK deps, Flatpak sandbox vs filesystem scanning), and standards (formats-as-contract, evdev key naming, axum body limits). Key findings: sqlx compile-time checks complicate the single-gate story, WebView2 is not guaranteed on all Windows 10 devices, and the deferred Tauri webview UI creates an explicit TypeScript boundary question for the designer. Every claim carries an inline source URL.
reply.commitMessage: docs: add research artifact for ADR-008 Rust product decision
docs: add design proposal for ADR-008 Rust product workspace

findings.location: Chosen design → "Formats contract: `schemas/` and the conformance harness" — "Reach-class tables are loaded from `schemas/` data by `bindforge-core`, per ADR-009." (also member table: `crates/core` owns "reach-table loader", "Created in: this design"; Test strategy #4)
findings.problem: The reach-table loader is created in this design and its data source is fixed, but its cost model is unstated: compile-time embedding vs runtime file read + TOML parse, and once-per-process vs per-call loading. Test #4's "into the in-memory model" implies load-once but the design never commits to it; a per-call read of `schemas/reach-classes/v1/` would put synchronous file IO and schema parsing on every resolution — the keystroke/event path, which the performance checklist treats as major — and a runtime read of repo paths also breaks in packaged deb/AppImage artifacts.
findings.fix: Amend the sentence to: reach-class tables are embedded into `bindforge-core` at compile time (e.g. `include_str!` of `schemas/reach-classes/v1/`) and parsed into the in-memory model once at process start; resolution touches only the in-memory tables, no file IO. This replaces the open-ended "loaded from `schemas/` data" phrasing; table contents remain deferred to ADR-009, only the load point is pinned.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — macOS row: "| macOS | unknown | BindForge commits nothing; Tauri v2 itself supports 10.15+ (A16); desktop design decides |" (same unknown in "| Contributor dev env | Linux + Windows yes; macOS unknown |")
findings.problem: A matrix row whose status is `unknown` is not a compatibility statement, and it contradicts the document's own Deferred section, which says macOS is "excluded for v1 per Compatibility matrix" while the matrix says unknown. The contributor cell's unknown also leaves a macOS contributor unable to tell whether the three cargo gate commands are expected to work for them.
findings.fix: Give both macOS cells a definite status without taking on macOS work: set the product row to `no (v1 decision)` (the status the Deferred text already claims) and the contributor row to `Linux + Windows yes; macOS no (v1)`; if macOS contributor builds are wanted instead, name a macOS leg in Test strategy #8.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix / Chosen design — no row or sentence names an OS input API (matrix has rows for Windows/Linux/Flatpak/macOS/CI only)
findings.problem: The checklist requires X11 vs Wayland vs Windows Raw Input vs macOS HID to be named per platform or the abstraction justified; the document never states which. Its own scope implies the answer — bindings travel as files under `schemas/` and `crates/scanner` does "installed-game detection, config fingerprinting (`compatdata` enumeration per A19)", i.e. file reads, not event capture — but the justification is absent, so a later reader cannot tell whether input capture is out of scope or unaddressed.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to the matrix notes (or Context): BindForge reads and writes binding files only and never reads or injects input events, so no X11/Wayland/Raw Input/HID API is targeted; any future component that captures input must name its API per platform in its own matrix.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix, Linux row — "| Linux (deb-based, WebKitGTK 4.1) | yes | dev deps per Tauri list (A16); shipping artifacts deb + AppImage |"
findings.problem: The row's support is scoped by packaging ("deb-based") while its own notes commit an AppImage artifact, which exists for non-deb distros, so the row both claims and contradicts deb-only support. Arch, Fedora and Steam Deck/SteamOS (read-only, not deb-based) get no status even though the Proton-prefix work that makes them relevant is in this design's member table ("`crates/scanner` … (`compatdata` enumeration per A19)").
findings.fix: Relabel the row to the platform set, e.g. "Linux (glibc distros; artifacts deb + AppImage)", and add a Steam Deck/SteamOS row with a status (`no (v1)` is fine if that is the decision) so the matrix states which Linux users get an artifact.

findings.location: Test strategy #8 — "the cargo gate must be green on the Linux CI runner; the `rust-toolchain.toml` auto-install is verified once on Linux and once on a Windows contributor machine during rollout"
findings.problem: The matrix claims Windows support twice ("Windows 10 (1803+) / 11 — desktop era | yes (target)" and "Contributor dev env | Linux + Windows yes"), but the only Windows platform check named is a rustup pin install; nothing establishes that `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace --locked` are green on Windows, where path-length limits and case-insensitive filesystems are exactly what a Linux-only gate first breaks on.
findings.fix: Add `windows-latest` to the `rust` job's runner matrix in `.github/workflows/check.yml` (or fold the same three commands into the one-time Windows verification in Rollout step 7), and say so in #8; otherwise downgrade the Windows contributor cell to `yes (toolchain only; gate unverified)`.

findings.location: Gates (ADR-008 clause 4), CI paragraph — "`orchestration` (`npm ci && npm run check` in `tools/orchestration`)"
findings.problem: This design creates the repo's first CI config (A23) and therefore owns the Node version running the pipeline gate, but no Node floor is named, so the gate silently changes Node version when the runner image updates — asymmetric with the Rust side, whose goal is "A toolchain floor and pin so every contributor and CI job builds identically" (`rust-version = "1.85"` plus `rust-toolchain.toml channel = "1.85.0"`).
findings.fix: Name the Node floor once: a `setup-node` step with an explicit `node-version` (or a root `.nvmrc` the job reads), recorded in the `repo-practices` section added by Rollout step 5. No Node API above a floor is introduced, so the finding is the missing floor, not a violation.

findings.location: Formats contract, Harness — "walks every `schemas/*/v*/fixtures/{valid,invalid}` directory" (and Test strategy #1)
findings.problem: The fixture tree and harness ship with this design, and per the matrix the harness also runs on contributor Windows (case-insensitive, path-length-limited) while CI runs only on Linux; nothing constrains fixture file names, so fixtures differing only in case, or using non-ASCII names, pass on Linux and silently collide or fail locally.
findings.fix: Add one clause to the versioning rule (mirrored in `schemas/README.md`): fixture file names are lowercase ASCII, `-`-separated, and case-unique within a fixture directory.

findings.location: Chosen design — Formats contract, "Adversarial guard": "Chain resolution hardened against adversarial profile files — the precondition for the hub validating uploads with client types"
findings.problem: The design creates the parser that consumes other people's files (bindforge-core is the reference implementation of schemas/, and the same compiled types validate hub uploads) but never classifies its data sources. It does not say that profile/patch/policy/manifest documents arriving from disk, from another user, or from the network are UNTRUSTED at every entry point, nor that Cycle/ChainTooDeep and the version gate apply regardless of entry point rather than only on the hub path. ADR-009, ADR-012 and ADR-014 all inherit that unstated premise, and the conformance harness as specified only ever parses in-repo trusted fixtures, so nothing in this design's own tests pins the untrusted-input contract.
findings.fix: Add one sentence at the head of "Adversarial guard": "profile, patch, policy, and manifest documents arriving from disk, from another user, or from the network are untrusted input at every entry point (CLI, desktop, hub); every guard in this section applies before any of them can reach a writer, and the invalid-fixture corpus is the contract for that behavior."

findings.location: Deferred / out of scope: "upload caps beyond the chain guard (file size, patch counts — axum body-limit posture)" — owned by ADR-014
findings.problem: The only input bound this design states is chain depth (MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH = 32). Size limits are deferred to ADR-014, which owns only the hub's HTTP body posture; the local path — CLI and desktop parsing a profile file from elsewhere, the product's primary use case — keeps no bound, and bindforge-core, created by this design, is that parser. An unbounded TOML document in size or table/array nesting can end a parse in an allocator or stack failure instead of a typed error, exactly the "reject cleanly, never crash" failure the section claims solved.
findings.fix: State an input budget in the same sentence as MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH and mirror it in schemas/README.md alongside the depth constant: a max document byte size and a max table/array nesting depth, both returned as typed errors, so the bound lives in core on every path and the ADR-014 body-limit deferral stops being load-bearing.

findings.location: Chosen design — "Versioning rule (canonical, mirrored in schemas/README.md)": "a document's declared version must name a major `crates/core` supports, else it is rejected with a structured error naming the supported majors"
findings.problem: The rule constrains only a declared version and never says what happens when the version field is absent or empty — the most common malformed-input case. Defaulting a missing version to v1 fails open: a document written against a future major is parsed with v1 semantics, which is precisely what versioning exists to prevent, and ADR-009's model can give future majors semantics v1 would misapply. Test strategy #2 covers only "declaring an unsupported major version", so the case is untested as well.
findings.fix: Extend the canonical rule to "a document that declares no version is rejected with the same structured error", add that case to Test strategy #2, and add a missing-version fixture under the affected format's fixtures/invalid/.

findings.location: Chosen design — "TypeScript boundary (clause 1; canonical)": "reached through Tauri commands gated by capabilities under `apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/` (A14)"
findings.problem: The capability model is named as the control that keeps the webview presentation-only, but the design never constrains what a capability file may grant. Tauri's advisory history shows plugin scopes are the weak seam: CVE-2022-46171 (fs scope glob too permissive), CVE-2022-41874 and CVE-2022-39215 (fs scope bypass, incl. symlink), CVE-2023-34460 (dotfile regression), and CVE-2025-31477 (tauri-plugin-shell `open` scope validation, CVSS 4.0, fixed only at 2.2.1). If the desktop design enables the fs/shell/dialog plugins — the default, easy path — the webview reads and writes game config files directly and the "presentation only" rule becomes decoration. A14 records only the opposite limitation (capabilities do not restrain Rust core code).
findings.fix: Add to the boundary paragraph, and to the repo-practices Rust section bullet in Rollout step 5: "capability files enumerate only the app's own commands; the fs, shell, and dialog plugins are not enabled — file access happens in workspace crates, never through plugin scopes."

findings.location: Assumption register A13 ("Tauri 2 is stable and current (2.12 line)") and members table ("apps/desktop … Tauri v2 app (A13)")
findings.problem: The design commits to Tauri v2 with no version floor. Advisory check (OSV/GitHub, crates.io) found CVE-2026-42184 / GHSA-7gmj-67g7-phm9: origin confusion letting a remote page invoke local-only IPC commands, affecting all >= 2.0.0, < 2.11.1, fixed in 2.11.1; CVE-2024-35222 (iFrames bypass the origin check guarding Tauri API access) is the same family. A13 says the 2.12 line is current but no patched floor is a requirement, so the desktop era could pin a stale 2.x and the capability boundary above would be bypassed at framework level.
findings.fix: One clause in the TypeScript boundary section: "capability-based isolation assumes a patched Tauri; the desktop design pins a tauri floor no lower than the release fixing its current IPC/origin advisories (2.11.1 as of this design) in [workspace.dependencies]."

findings.location: Chosen design — "Gates (ADR-008 clause 4)": "cargo fmt --all -- --check / cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings / cargo test --workspace --locked"
findings.problem: Neither the gate set nor the repo-practices section keeps dependency advisories under watch, even though this design fixes the gate set, pins exact versions, and leaves A25 unverified. The committed Cargo.lock plus --locked make the full graph known — exactly what an advisory scan needs — yet the only check on the graph is a human reviewing an upgrade PR.
findings.fix: Add a fourth line to the gate block and the CI rust job: `cargo deny check advisories` with a committed deny.toml at the workspace root (cargo-audit as the fallback), rather than leaving advisory review informal.

findings.location: Chosen design — "Workspace shape": "the channel equals `rust-version` and is bumped only when a reviewed dependency upgrade requires it"
findings.problem: The only sanctioned reason to move the pinned 1.85.0 channel is a dependency demand, so a rustc security advisory with a patch release has no defined path and contributors stay on a pinned compiler because the policy forbids moving it.
findings.fix: Widen the clause to "bumped only when a reviewed dependency upgrade or a published security advisory in the toolchain requires it" — the sentence currently forbids the obvious case; no new mechanism is needed.

findings.location: Chosen design — "Gates": "`.github/workflows/check.yml` runs two independent jobs on every PR"
findings.problem: This is the repo's first CI config (A23), so its permissions posture is this design's to set, and the rust job compiles contributor-authored code on every PR: build scripts and proc macros in a PR's dependency graph execute arbitrary code on the runner. The design specifies commands but no runner posture.
findings.fix: One sentence in the same paragraph, before Rollout step 4: "check.yml declares permissions: contents: read at the job level and pins every third-party action to a commit SHA; PR-triggered runs get no write token."

findings.location: Chosen design — "Harness": "walks every `schemas/*/v*/fixtures/{valid,invalid}` directory, and asserts: every valid fixture parses and re-serializes to a semantically equal value; every invalid fixture is rejected"
findings.problem: An empty or absent directory satisfies this trivially, so a format added later with no fixtures — or fixtures moved out of the expected glob — passes the gate while contributing zero conformance. Because the versioning rule makes "a file's presence in vN/fixtures/valid/ … the definition of 'supported'", silent emptiness silently un-supports a format. The "at least one valid and one invalid fixture per format" requirement is prose in this section and Test strategy #1, not asserted by the harness.
findings.fix: Make conformance.rs fail when any schemas/*/v*/ directory yields zero valid or zero invalid fixtures, so the assertion replaces the prose promise instead of sitting beside it.

findings.location: Deferred / out of scope — the list names owners for semantics, codecs, hub policy, packaging and schemas, but none for what a shared artifact reveals
findings.problem: No document is named as owning what a shared BindForge artifact reveals about its author: crates/scanner enumerates compatdata (A19), i.e. installed-game titles, and adapters' "config path discovery" puts absolute host paths into data the product exists to share. Nothing records which of ADR-009 (manifest contents) or ADR-012 (fingerprinting) carries the "what may leave the machine, and what may a log contain" decision, so it can fall between them.
findings.fix: Add one Deferred bullet naming the owner: ADR-009 for manifest and scanner-derived fields identifying the user or host, ADR-012 for path redaction during fingerprinting. No new requirements.

findings.location: Deferred / out of scope: "Codec implementations, config path discovery, write policy, and conformance obligations for third-party game formats (INI/TOML/UTF-16 round-trips) — owned by ADR-012 (planned)"
findings.problem: The deferral is consistent with ADR-008 clause 2, so it is not re-opened; but the security obligation inside it is unnamed and may be lost when ADR-012 is drafted.
findings.fix: Extend that bullet's wording with "including path canonicalization and rejection of .. and absolute paths arriving from untrusted profile data, and never interpolating paths into shell strings".

findings.location: Chosen design — "Formats contract: `schemas/` and the conformance harness": "The scaffold ships with at least one valid and one invalid fixture per format; ADR-009's build seeds the real cases." (repeated in Test strategy #1 and Rollout 3)
findings.problem: The harness asserts every valid fixture "parses and re-serializes to a semantically equal value", so the first merged slice must implement working parse+serialize for all four formats (profile, patch, manifest, policy) — while Rollout 2 creates `crates/core` as a "package skeleton" whose "public APIs and model content follow ADR-009" and Non-goals hand "chains, policies, manifest contents" to ADR-009. The slice either invents four format models now and re-does them when ADR-009 lands, or the scaffold fixtures are placeholders and Test #1/#5 pass vacuously. Either way it is more model implementation than ADR-008's four clauses require, and it duplicates ownership of that surface with ADR-009.
findings.fix: Narrow the three sentences (Harness, Test #1, Rollout 3) to the formats this design's own Goals exercise — `profile/v1` (needed by `resolve_chain` and the chain-guard fixtures) and `schemas/reach-classes/v1/` — and state that the other three format directories arrive with ADR-009, picked up automatically by the harness's existing `schemas/*/v*/fixtures/{valid,invalid}` walk with no code change. This removes work instead of adding a mechanism.

findings.location: Chosen design — "Workspace shape", root Cargo.toml: "opt-level = 3                       # A6; applies once from the workspace root", plus "clap = { version = \"4.6.7\", features = [\"derive\"] }" and "toml_edit = \"0.25\""
findings.problem: A build profile and dependency entries with no consumer in this design: nothing in the slice uses sqlx (the adjacent comment itself defers "axum, sqlx (A2, A3) enter [workspace.dependencies] with the hub era"), `clap` is consumed only by `apps/cli` (ADR-012), and `toml_edit`'s justification — comment-preserving writes — is the codec/write-policy work Deferred to ADR-012; reading `schemas/` TOML needs only a plain serde TOML reader. Config knobs and deps ahead of their consumers (checklist items 4 and 6).
findings.fix: Delete the `[profile.dev.package.sqlx-macros]` block and the `clap`/`toml_edit` lines from the root Cargo.toml in this design; each is added by the ADR that creates its first consumer, which the existing "Later, with the hub era" rollout line already instructs.

findings.location: Chosen design — Gates, "Canonical sqlx rule (hub-era; everything else cross-references this)": "`SQLX_OFFLINE` is irrelevant until `apps/hub` exists."
findings.problem: The paragraph specifies the full hub-era mechanism (committed root `.sqlx/`, `cargo sqlx prepare --workspace` per PR, `SQLX_OFFLINE=true` in every gate job, a dedicated Postgres `--check` job), and Test strategy #7 plus a Risks row carry it, yet a workspace with no sqlx member needs no DB by construction. This is a future document's design written down here, and it is not in the Deferred list (which sends hub schema, migrations and upload caps to ADR-014 but not this) — a larger design than the Goals need (checklist items 3 and 5).
findings.fix: Keep the one-sentence decision in Options considered (offline cache over Postgres-service or macro ban) and move the mechanism wording, Test #7 and the risk row into the existing ADR-014 Deferred bullet, appending "plus the sqlx offline cache and its `--check` job".

findings.location: Options considered — "Flatpak in the packaging matrix: ship or exclude." and Compatibility matrix row "Windows 10 (1803+) / 11 — desktop era"
findings.problem: This design decides Flatpak exclusion, NSIS-vs-MSI, WebView2 pre-install posture and macOS/Android status, and carries assumptions A13–A19 (Tauri, WebView2 distribution, Flatpak sandbox, Proton paths) for a surface its Non-goals assign to "the desktop design" and its Deferred list already defers with "no follow-up yet". One option entry, four matrix rows and one risk row are spent outside the Goals; the smaller design named by checklist item 3 keeps workspace, gates, `schemas/` harness and the TypeScript boundary only.
findings.fix: Collapse the Flatpak option entry and the Windows/macOS/Android/Flatpak rows into one matrix row ("desktop packaging — the desktop design decides") or a one-line decision note, and drop assumptions A13–A19 unless a surviving row cites them.

findings.location: Non-goals — "The model's semantics (taxonomy, reach tables, chains, policies, manifest contents) — owned by ADR-009." vs Chosen design — Adversarial guard: "`ChainTooDeep` (chain longer than `MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH = 32`) … the constant is documented in `schemas/README.md` so third-party readers can conform"
findings.problem: Chain semantics are declared out of scope, but this design fixes a normative depth cap, publishes it as part of the third-party conformance contract, and Test #3 freezes the boundary at exactly 32. Two documents own one public number, and no text gives a basis for 32, so ADR-009 inherits a constraint it was told it owns.
findings.fix: Add one clause to the Adversarial guard paragraph: chain semantics are ADR-009's, and this design fixes only the two error variant names and where the constant lives; either state the basis for 32 or mark it "initial value, ADR-009 may set it", and pin Test #3 to the constant rather than the literal 32.

findings.location: Chosen design — "Workspace shape": "[workspace.lints.rust]" and "[workspace.lints.clippy]" (both empty) next to the claim "the floor and lint policy are declared exactly once"
findings.problem: The two lint tables contain no entries, so no lint policy is actually declared, and the gate already escalates with `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`. An abstraction with no consumer behind it (checklist item 6).
findings.fix: Omit both tables until a specific lint belongs there (e.g. an `unused = "deny"` entry), or name the one lint they hold.

findings.location: Chosen design — member table: "`crates/transforms` | `bindforge-transforms` | policy stacks | this design; contents per ADR-009"
findings.problem: A second empty workspace member created now; no Goal, the harness, or the gate exercises it, and the `members = ["crates/*"]` glob already accepts it unchanged whenever content exists.
findings.fix: Create `crates/transforms` in the ADR-009 slice, or keep the row and state plainly that it is a placeholder the gate compiles empty.

findings.location: Chosen design → Workspace shape, root Cargo.toml block: `license = "MIT"          # matches LICENSE + tools/orchestration (A23)`
findings.problem: The claim is false. The repo's LICENSE file is the Apache License 2.0 text, while tools/orchestration/package.json:29 declares "license": "MIT" — the repo is already split, and A23's recorded basis ("repo listing 2026-11-11; tools/orchestration/package.json:23") covers only the absence of the product tree and the npm check script, so nothing cited supports the license half of this row. Rollout step 1 copies the block verbatim, so the design commits every crate to MIT against an Apache-2.0 LICENSE.
findings.fix: Set `license = "Apache-2.0"` to match LICENSE (or record an explicit relicensing decision) and replace the comment with a citation of the two license files, or a new register row, instead of A23; record the package.json-MIT vs LICENSE-Apache-2.0 mismatch as a separate repo fix rather than papering over it.

findings.location: Chosen design → "Adversarial guard" vs Non-goals ("The model's semantics (taxonomy, reach tables, chains, policies, manifest contents) — owned by ADR-009") and Deferred ("chain/patch/policy/manifest semantics and their fixture cases — owned by ADR-009")
findings.problem: This design simultaneously defers chain semantics to ADR-009 and decides them: it fixes `ChainTooDeep` "(chain longer than `MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH = 32`)", puts the constant in `schemas/README.md` "so third-party readers can conform", and Test strategy #3 places chain-boundary fixtures under `schemas/profile/v1/fixtures/invalid/` in the scaffold. An implementer cannot tell which document owns the depth bound, its error variants, and their fixtures — the guard is the one piece of chain semantics that must be a public cross-language contract here.
findings.fix: One sentence in the guard paragraph: the bound and the `Cycle`/`ChainTooDeep` variants are decided by this design and are a constraint ADR-009 must adopt; then narrow the Deferred/Non-goals clause to "chain semantics other than the depth guard and its boundary fixtures".

findings.location: Chosen design → Workspace shape, root Cargo.toml: `members = ["crates/*", "apps/*"]` with no `resolver`
findings.problem: The block is a virtual manifest, and the Cargo page A7 cites says a virtual workspace must set `resolver` explicitly because it has no `package.edition` to infer it from. As committed, cargo warns on every command and falls back to the edition-independent resolver, silently splitting feature unification across core/transforms — against the stated goal that workspace policy is "declared exactly once".
findings.fix: Add `resolver = "3"` to `[workspace]` in the block (it is copied verbatim in Rollout step 1).

findings.location: Chosen design → Workspace shape, `[workspace.dependencies]`: `serde = { features = ["derive"] }   # exact version pinned at merge`
findings.problem: A workspace dependency entry needs a source, and the cited Cargo reference states that members inheriting a workspace dependency "cannot use any other dependency key (such as `version`)" — no member can supply the pin later, so the committed block is not a resolvable manifest.
findings.fix: Give the floor now (`serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }`), or drop the entry and say it lands with the first crate that needs serde.

findings.location: Chosen design → Workspace shape members note: "(the `crates/*` and `apps/*` globs follow A7's flat-members recommendation)" vs table row `apps/desktop` → "`src-tauri` package `bindforge-desktop`"
findings.problem: `apps/*` matches one path segment, so a crate at `apps/desktop/src-tauri` is never matched by the committed globs; the workspace silently drops a member when the desktop era lands. The TypeScript boundary defers the exact `members` path but never says the glob cannot reach it.
findings.fix: Add a clause to the members note: the desktop era adds an explicit `members` entry for the `src-tauri` path, since the flat globs will not match it.

findings.location: Formats contract → harness paragraph: "walks every `schemas/*/v*/fixtures/{valid,invalid}` directory, and asserts: every valid fixture parses and re-serializes to a semantically equal value"
findings.problem: The tree gives `reach-classes/v1/` only "tables as TOML data + fixtures/" with no valid/invalid split, and Test strategy #4 tests reach tables through a separate loader contract. The glob either sweeps reach-class data into a round-trip assertion that is undefined for it, or matches nothing and the directory goes unexercised — an unevaluated empty/absent-input edge case.
findings.fix: Give `reach-classes/v1/` the same `fixtures/valid` + `fixtures/invalid` layout and state that table data is asserted by load + per-hand distinctness (Test #4), not by re-serialization.

findings.location: Formats contract → versioning rule: "a file's presence in `vN/fixtures/valid/` is the definition of \"supported\"" next to rejection "with a structured error naming the supported majors"
findings.problem: Two definitions of "supported" — repo-side fixture directories and a compiled-in list in bindforge-core — with nothing in Test strategy keeping them equal, and the rule never says what happens to a document that declares no version at all.
findings.fix: Add a test asserting core's declared supported majors equal the majors present under `schemas/*/v*`, and state that an absent version declaration is a structured rejection, with a fixture under `schemas/profile/v1/fixtures/invalid/`.

findings.location: Assumption register A2: "axum 0.8.9 ships, MSRV 1.80, breaking 0.9 in dev, consumes `tower` | verified"
findings.problem: The cited README supports MSRV 1.80, 0.9-in-dev and tower, but only states that the `0.8.x` branch is what is released to crates.io — it does not support the exact patch 0.8.9.
findings.fix: Cite crates.io/docs.rs for the patch number, or write "0.8.x".

findings.location: Assumption register A16: "WebView2 is preinstalled on Windows 10 (1803+) and 11 but \"some devices might not\" have it ... | verified | https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/"
findings.problem: The quoted phrase is not on the cited Tauri prerequisites page (it says WebView2 "is already installed on Windows 10 (from version 1803 onward)"); the sentence appears on the WebView2 distribution page cited by A17.
findings.fix: Attribute the quote to the A17 URL instead of the prerequisites page.

findings.location: Gates → canonical sqlx rule: "every gate job builds with `SQLX_OFFLINE=true` and no `DATABASE_URL`; a dedicated hub-path CI job with a Postgres service runs `cargo sqlx prepare --check --workspace`"
findings.problem: The sqlx-cli README states all sqlx commands require a database URL, so the hub-path `prepare --check` job cannot be one of the jobs described as building with no `DATABASE_URL`; the two sentences overlap as written.

findings.location: Chosen design → Workspace shape / Gates / Test strategy #5 — "`rust-toolchain.toml` with `[toolchain] channel = "1.85.0"`" … "`rust` (the three gate commands above, and nothing installed beyond the pinned toolchain (A11))" … "every command listed in the Gates block succeeds … with nothing installed beyond the pinned toolchain"
findings.problem: New in this revision: the revised text makes "nothing installed beyond the pinned toolchain" load-bearing — it is the stated reason advisory scanning is excluded and now part of Test #5's one-gate promise — but two of the three gate commands depend on rustup components that the committed `channel` pin does not name: `cargo fmt` needs `rustfmt`, `cargo clippy` needs `clippy`. They are present only because rustup's default install profile happens to include them, so a `--profile minimal` contributor install (or any toolchain installed without those components) fails the gate for a setup reason, not a code reason. A11's basis covers the channel pin only. The three prior compatibility findings (gate-tool acquisition, unassigned Windows verification, Postgres row exercise) are all closed: the gate is back to the three toolchain-shipped commands, Rollout 7 schedules the Windows leg of Test #7, and the Postgres row cites ADR-014's strategy; dropping `cargo deny` does not contradict ADR-008 clause 4, which fixes only clippy + fmt as the check gate. Fix: name the components beside the channel in Workspace shape — `[toolchain] channel = "1.85.0"` plus `components = ["clippy", "rustfmt"]` — so the "nothing installed beyond the pinned toolchain" claim is guaranteed by the committed file instead of by the installer's default profile.
findings.fix: Extend the `rust-toolchain.toml` contents in Workspace shape to declare `components = ["clippy", "rustfmt"]` alongside `channel = "1.85.0"`; this replaces the reliance on rustup's default install profile that Gates and Test #5 now assert away.

findings.location: Chosen design → Gates / Test strategy #5 — Gates: "`rust` (the three gate commands above, and nothing installed beyond the pinned toolchain (A11))"; #5: "every command listed in the Gates block succeeds on the Linux CI runner, with nothing installed beyond the pinned toolchain"
findings.problem: new: the added "nothing installed beyond the pinned toolchain" promise holds only if the pinned toolchain carries rustfmt and clippy. The toolchain file this design fixes ("`rust-toolchain.toml` with `[toolchain] channel = \"1.85.0\"`", copied verbatim in Rollout 1) requests no components, and rustup installs a toolchain-file toolchain with the machine's configured profile — the rustup toolchain-file page notes the profile falls back to a possibly-changed default, and the profiles page recommends the `minimal` profile "in CI" (and on Windows); minimal ships only rustc, rust-std, cargo, so `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` fail on such a clone. Test #5's one-gate promise and Test #7's Windows/contributor leg therefore depend on an environment setting the design never decides.
findings.fix: Make the components explicit in the Workspace shape toolchain file: `[toolchain] channel = "1.85.0"` plus `components = ["rustfmt", "clippy"]` (additive regardless of profile). No other text changes.

findings.location: Chosen design — "Gates (ADR-008 clause 4)": "Per-PR dependency-advisory scanning is deliberately excluded from the gate: it needs a tool outside the pinned toolchain and an advisory database that is live network state" (and Deferred: "Dependency-advisory scanning (`cargo deny`, a root `deny.toml`) — no follow-up yet")
findings.problem: Regression: the r1 text I approved carried a standing dependency-advisory control (`cargo deny check advisories` against the committed `Cargo.lock`, with `deny.toml` created in Rollout 1). This pass removes it from the gate, from Rollout 1, and from the Revision log's closure, and hands the obligation to a Deferred bullet that names no owner and no cadence — every other Deferred bullet names the document that inherits its concern, this one says "no follow-up yet", so no mechanism and no party in the run ever looks at advisories for a lockfile this design commits and freezes with `--locked`. The design still depends on advisory information existing: `rust-toolchain.toml` is bumped when "a published toolchain security advisory requires it" (Workspace shape), and the TypeScript boundary's numeric floor is justified as the "current fix for the IPC-origin advisories". That justification is already stale on the framework ADR-008 fixes: Tauri GHSA-w28w-mhc8-qvjv ("Improper Tauri IPC Access Control for Fetch Command", high, CVSS 7.6, published 2026-09-26) covers >= 2.0.0, <= 2.11.5 and is patched only at 2.11.6 — above the 2.11.1 floor this design publishes — and it exists only as a Tauri-repository advisory, absent from crates.io OSV/RustSec, so the deleted `cargo deny` gate could not have surfaced it either. Net effect: the automated half of the approved posture is gone and the human half was never added. (Separately confirmed, not a blocker: no dependency at the design's stated versions carries a known unfixed advisory — RUSTSEC-2024-0363 is fixed at sqlx 0.8.1 vs the design's 0.9, and CVE-2026-42184/GHSA-7gmj-67g7-phm9 is fixed at tauri 2.11.1, matching the floor.) Label: regression.
findings.fix: Keep the author's objection to the placement — advisory scanning stays out of the three-command per-PR gate — but replace "no follow-up yet" with an owner: rewrite the Deferred bullet to name a scheduled, non-PR-blocking workflow running `cargo deny check advisories` against the committed lock with a root `deny.toml`, and add one clause to TypeScript boundary: "the desktop design pins the newest `tauri` release available when it lands and checks the framework's own security-advisory list, not only crates.io". No new tooling; if the scheduled job is rejected, the bullet must instead name who checks advisories and on what trigger — the sentence replaces the unowned deferral rather than adding to it.

That new external claim is registered as A27, verified against the Tauri advisory (GHSA-w28w-mhc8-qvjv, `>= 2.0.0, <= 2.11.5`, patched only 2.11.6) and an OSV crates.io query showing no such entry; the false 'also in Rollout 5' cross-reference was dropped. findings.problem: new — the closure dropped the stale justification but kept the stale number as the floor. A27 in the same document records GHSA-w28w-mhc8-qvjv (High, CVSS 7.6, verified live: affected >= 2.0.0, <= 2.11.5, patched >= 2.11.6), so the floor explicitly permits 2.11.1–2.11.5, and that advisory's mechanism is exactly the control this paragraph relies on: `plugin:__TAURI_CHANNEL__|fetch` is carved out of Tauri's ACL rejection branch, queue is app-wide with old monotonic u32 ids, so a renderer retrieves queued IPC payloads belonging to another webview with no capability check. A floor's only job is to catch downgrades, and this one sits below the patch for the High-severity IPC advisory the paragraph itself cites. Separately, "newest `tauri` release available" is ambiguous when read: the newest published `tauri` on crates.io today is 3.0.0-alpha.6 while the newest stable v2 is 2.12.5, and ADR-008 clause 2 fixes "Tauri v2", so a literal reading pins an unreleased major's alpha.
findings.fix: Change the parenthetical to "(never below 2.11.6, the patch A27 names)" and qualify the pin as "the newest stable v2 release available when it lands". This replaces the 2.11.1 floor rather than adding a second constraint.

findings.location: crates/core/src/toml.rs:60
findings.problem: Per-line `Vec<char>` allocation on the untrusted-document parse path (the hub upload-validation path the design names): every parsed line allocates a fresh 4-bytes-per-char buffer, and a 1 MiB single-line document forces one ~4 MiB allocation on top of the document. Bounded by MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES, so not blocking, but avoidable.
findings.fix: Scan `trimmed.as_bytes()` with byte-indexed positions instead of collecting into `Vec<char>`; all structural grammar characters are ASCII and no UTF-8 continuation byte is ASCII, so byte-level scanning is correct while string contents are still collected as chars.

findings.location: crates/core/src/toml.rs:75
findings.problem: `entries.insert(key.clone(), value)` clones every key on every entry; the clone exists only to keep `key` available for the duplicate-key error message on line 78, so the accept path wastes an allocation per entry.
findings.fix: Use the entry API: `match entries.entry(key) { Occupied(e) => Err(... using e.key() ...), Vacant(v) => v.insert(value) }`.

findings.location: crates/core/src/document.rs:91
findings.problem: `supported_majors()` builds a fresh `Vec<String>` (heap `String` per major) on every parse call, including the accept path's version comparison; a rejecting document allocates it up to three times (lines 86, 91, 94).
findings.fix: Compare `version != MAJOR_V1` directly against the constant and build the `supported` vector only inside the error branches.

findings.location: crates/core/src/toml.rs:201-224
findings.problem: `parse_integer` accumulates digits into a `String` and, for negatives, `format!("-{digits}")` allocates again before `parse::<i64>()`; every integer in a document pays an unnecessary allocation.
findings.fix: Accumulate the value arithmetically with checked overflow (replacing the `parse` map_err refusal) and apply the sign at the end.

findings.location: crates/core/src/document.rs:243-258
findings.problem: `quoted()` escapes only `"`, `\`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t` and pushes every other char raw, so an id containing a control char the reader decodes (`\b` → U+0008, `\f` → U+000C, src/toml.rs:161-162) re-serializes into text its own reader rejects (src/toml.rs:175) and no TOML v1.1 reader accepts. This breaks the contract's "valid fixture re-serializes to a semantically equal value" promise (schemas/README.md, schemas/profile/v1/spec.md:50-51); no shipped fixture triggers it, so the gate stays green.
findings.fix: Encode remaining chars < 0x20 (and 0x7F) as `\u00XX` in `quoted()`, and add a profile/v1/fixtures/valid/ fixture whose id uses such an escape so the round trip is covered by the corpus.

findings.location: crates/core/src/toml.rs:155-173
findings.problem: The v1 grammar never pins the string-escape set (schemas/README.md and both spec.md say only "quoted string"), and the reader refuses TOML v1.1's `\uXXXX`/`\UXXXXXXXX`. A third-party writer that escapes non-ASCII emits a document bindforge-core rejects, while bindforge-core writes non-ASCII literally — so non-ASCII binding names survive the format in one direction only, and the asymmetry is invisible to implementers and untested by the corpus.
findings.fix: Accept `\uXXXX`/`\UXXXXXXXX` (rejecting lone surrogates and code points above U+10FFFF), or state the exact permitted escape set in schemas/README.md and both spec.md files and add an invalid fixture for `\u`.

findings.location: .github/workflows/check.yml:25-30
findings.problem: README.md:21-23 and .opencode/skills/repo-practices/SKILL.md:53-58 (and the proposal's Workspace shape, A8/A11) promise "Cargo.lock is committed; CI uses `--locked`", but only the test step passes it. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` runs first without `--locked`, so a resolution change rewrites Cargo.lock inside the job and the later `cargo test --locked` verifies the already-mutated lock; the gate can pass on a dependency graph no contributor has, on every platform.
findings.fix: Use `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` (fmt resolves no graph), or record in Gates and repo-practices that only cargo test is locked and why.

findings.location: .gitattributes (absent at repo root)
findings.problem: The Compatibility matrix commits to a Windows contributor dev env and this change makes schemas/**/*.toml a byte-level contract, but no line-ending policy is pinned: a Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true yields CRLF contract trees and sources. It works only by accident (the reader tolerates CRLF via str::lines() + trim in src/toml.rs:46-48, and that tolerance is not stated in the contract), and rustfmt's default newline_style="Auto" is platform-native, so `cargo fmt` on Windows rewrites every .rs file to CRLF.
findings.fix: Add .gitattributes (`*.rs text eol=lf`, `*.toml text eol=lf`, or `* text=auto eol=lf`) and one line in schemas/README.md stating the line-ending rule implementers must accept.

findings.location: crates/core/tests/conformance.rs:144-164
findings.problem: The only guard aimed at filesystem case sensitivity is unreachable: the preceding assertion (conformance.rs:137-141) already forces every fixture name segment to lowercase ASCII via is_fixture_name (tests/common/mod.rs:191-205), so no surviving name can collide case-insensitively; the lowercased sort/dedup check can never fail.
findings.fix: Either drop the dedup check and note that the lowercase rule is itself the collision guard, or allow case-unique mixed-case names so the check does real work.

findings.location: rust-toolchain.toml:6-7
findings.problem: The gate needs the rustfmt and clippy components, but the toolchain file pins only `channel`; the one-gate promise (Test strategy #5, "nothing installed beyond the pinned toolchain") therefore depends on rustup's default `recommended` profile, and a `--profile minimal` contributor or image fails on an unchanged PR.
findings.fix: Add `components = ["rustfmt", "clippy"]` to the `[toolchain]` table.

findings.location: crates/core/src/document.rs:144-201
findings.problem: The reference parser silently accepts any number of unknown top-level entries, contradicting the grammar tables shipped in the same diff (schemas/profile/v1/spec.md:22 and schemas/reach-classes/v1/spec.md:30: "Any other entry is rejected"). This is the one place bindforge-core is more permissive than the contract it is the reference for, it runs against the Adversarial-guard premise that the invalid-fixture corpus is the contract for rejection behavior, and no invalid fixture exercises an unknown entry, so crates/core/tests/conformance.rs:77-93 cannot detect it. A third-party reader written from spec.md rejects documents the hub-side reference implementation accepts.
findings.fix: After the required entries are read, reject every key outside the format's grammar table with a typed CoreError (InvalidValue { key, message: "not part of the <format>/v1 grammar" } or a dedicated UnknownEntry variant), and add schemas/profile/v1/fixtures/invalid/unknown-entry.toml and schemas/reach-classes/v1/fixtures/invalid/unknown-entry.toml so the corpus pins the rule for every implementer.

findings.location: crates/core/src/toml.rs:38-83 (also toml.rs:52-58, toml.rs:251)
findings.problem: The proposal fixes the contract as "Formats are TOML (ADR-009) over TOML v1.1.0 (A20)", but the in-tree reader accepts a hand-rolled line-oriented subset and rejects legal TOML v1.1.0 — table headers, dotted keys, multi-line arrays, floats, hex integers. That narrows which documents the language-neutral contract admits: anyone using a standard TOML parser (ADR-009/ADR-012 authors, third-party readers) accepts a multi-line `derives = [...]` profile that bindforge-core refuses with Malformed. The narrowing is stated only in the new contract-tree docs (schemas/README.md:31-38, the two spec.md grammar sections), not against the proposal's format claim, and this seat could not confirm it is recorded in 03-build-notes.md.
findings.fix: Either declare the subset as a deviation in 03-build-notes.md with the dependency-free reason and reword schemas/README.md to say the v1 grammar is a subset of TOML v1.1.0 (not "TOML over TOML v1.1.0"), or parse with the real `toml` crate and keep the subset as fixture guidance only. If the build notes already record it, this reduces to the README wording.

findings.location: crates/core/tests/conformance.rs:56-60
findings.problem: Valid reach-classes fixtures are parsed and then skipped with `continue`, so they are never load-asserted. The proposal ("Reach-class table fixtures are asserted by load + distinctness (Test strategy #4)") and the spec shipped in this diff (schemas/reach-classes/v1/spec.md:41-44) both promise a load assertion, while reach_tables.rs:26-31 loads only the version directory's left.toml/right.toml data. Per-hand distinctness is pinned for the data files and lost for the corpus that ADR-009 will extend.
findings.fix: For each reach-classes/v1/fixtures/valid/ fixture, assert the parsed document is a ReachClassTable whose hand matches the harness expectation (or drive load_reach_tables over a temp directory holding the fixture), keeping the invalid-fixture rejection; or record in 03-build-notes.md that the scaffold asserts those fixtures by parse + guard only and correct the spec wording to match.

findings.location: .github/workflows/advisories.yml:63-65 (with :66-74)
findings.problem: Round-1's dead control is still open, by a new mechanism. The flag order is now correct — in cargo-deny 0.20.2 `Arg::new("FORMAT")` is defined on the top-level Command (Args::command()) without global propagation, and check's Args::cmd() has no `--format`, so `cargo deny --format json check` parses — but the redirect still captures nothing. In 0.20.2 every `--format json` record goes to stderr: common.rs DiagPrinter::new builds `OutputFormat::Json(Json { stream: StdioStream::Err(std::io::stderr()) })` (StdioStream has no stdout variant), OutputLock::Json serializes diagnostic packs into that stderr lock, setup_logger(Format::Json) chains log records to stderr, and stats.rs print_stats writes the {"type":"summary"} record to stderr ("for JSON we still go to stderr"); stdout receives only --audit-compat printlns and SARIF. So `> cargo-deny-report.json` leaves a 0-byte file, `[ ! -s ]` fires, and the weekly job is red forever with no report artifact: the design's only recurring look at the lockfile (advisories, bans, licenses, sources) still produces nothing to triage and the rust-toolchain security-advisory bump trigger stays unmet. The failure is also now misleading — `::error::cargo-deny produced no report; the scheduled lockfile scan did not run` is false, since the scan ran and its findings were dropped on stderr — and the step comment at :51-62 asserts the report 'still has to exist', arguing for behavior the pinned tool does not have.
findings.fix: Capture the stream the pinned tool actually writes its report to, and test content rather than size. findings.location: crates/core/tests/common/mod.rs:203-211
findings.problem: ScratchDir::write now calls fs::create_dir_all(path.parent()) with no confinement check on the caller-supplied `name`. Because the path is built with Path::join, an absolute `name` replaces the scratch base and a `..`-carrying name walks outside it; previously the bare fs::write usually failed at ENOENT on the missing parent, which incidentally fenced such a walk. With parents auto-created, a future suite can create directories and write files outside the scratch tree, where Drop (which removes only self.path, lines 214-218) will not clean them up — and this helper is the one every new suite copies. All 14 current write/make_dir call sites pass compile-time relative literals with no `..` and no absolute path, and no untrusted data reaches the helper, so this is hardening of the test sandbox rather than a live hole; it is the only security-relevant effect of the post-approval revision, which otherwise broke nothing I approved.
findings.fix: On the next touch of this helper, confine the join: panic on an absolute `name` or one containing a Component::ParentDir (std::path::Component check on Path::new(name)), or assert the resulting path still starts with self.path before calling create_dir_all/fs::write, and state that contract in the doc comment.
